title: Semiclassical dynamics of higher-order squeezing: self-adjoint extensions and coherent returns
abstract: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians have several self-adjoint realizations, while their classical trajectories reach infinity in finite time. We relate these extension problems through boundary amplitudes and the semiclassical propagation of coherent states. A discrete Fourier transformation gives the sink-to-source ray matrix of each quantum realization. After the first passage through infinity, the full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, with weights equal to the squared moduli of the matrix entries. The proof combines finite-order approximate tail solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition with full-norm Gaussian matching and a square-summable residual estimate. For positive energy, we determine the limit after any fixed number of passages: amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix. We also realize these limits by concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension, distinguishing deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the semiclassical dynamics of quantum systems described by higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians whose classical paths blow up in finite time. It rigorously determines the required self-adjoint extensions by relating quantum propagation to classical boundary amplitudes. The key finding is that the quantum probability measure concentrates on outgoing classical branches, revealing a coherent evolution structure beyond simple stochastic mixing.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the semiclassical dynamics of higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians, specifically addressing the mathematical necessity of defining self-adjoint extensions because classical trajectories escape to infinity in finite time.
main_result: The full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches after the first passage through infinity, and for positive energy, amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix.
method: The analysis combines relating extension problems via boundary amplitudes, using a discrete Fourier transformation to find a sink-to-source ray matrix, and employing Gaussian matching techniques.
model_or_system: The system is governed by a higher-order squeezing Hamiltonian, $H_k(q, p)$, whose classical dynamics lead to finite-time escape. The quantum dynamics are analyzed using the Liouville operator and coherent state propagation.
key_observables: Husimi probability measure, boundary amplitudes, sink-to-source ray matrix, and coherent state evolution $\psi_{\hbar}(t)$.
important_parameters: Squeezing order $k > 2$, energy $c$, and the semiclassical parameter $\hbar$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on constructing approximate solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition, and the analysis distinguishes deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.
figures_summary: Figures compare the quantum Husimi density to classical transport using coherent Liouville amplitudes, showing how the limiting first-pass weights match between quantum and coherent classical descriptions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the Hamiltonian and the problem of self-adjoint extensions, developing the semiclassical machinery using ray matrices and Gaussian matching, and finally establishing the limiting behavior of the quantum measure compared to classical transport.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools for understanding quantum dynamics in regimes where standard semiclassical approximations fail due to finite-time singularities, which is crucial for modeling complex quantum optical or many-body interactions.
